title: Correctness of a nonbad decision
statement: Let $n\ge 0$, let $P$ be a set of coordinates among the $n$ inputs, and fix signs on the coordinates in $P$. Let the target be a function from the sign cube ${-1,1}^n$ to $	ext{signs }{pm1}$. A decision is either that the target restricted to the remaining coordinates is constant at a specified sign, or that it depends on a specified remaining coordinate. If this decision is not bad—that is, it is not incorrect—then it is correct: in the constant case the restriction equals the specified constant function, and in the coordinate case the restriction genuinely depends on that coordinate.
hypotheses_covered: A fixed coordinate set $P$ among the $n$ input coordinates
The decision is not bad, meaning it is not incorrect
